blind.description: A stylized stone ossuary shelving unit built from chunky, bevelled masonry blocks. The unit has four tiers: the top shelf is empty with small triangular cobwebs in the rear corners, the second shelf holds five neatly aligned humanoid skulls, the third shelf holds stacked long bones, and the bottom shelf is filled with more stacked leg bones. The frame consists of two thick side pillars made of stacked stone blocks, a solid stone back panel, and stone shelf dividers. The material is stylized weathered brown-grey stone with warm tan/bone-colored skeletal remains.
blind.from_above: A wide rectangular frame composed of square stone corner pillars on the left and right connected by a segmented rear wall ledge, looking down onto the flat recessed stone surface of the top shelf with subtle cobwebs in the inner back corners.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 4.8 to 5.0 ft tall (reaching roughly to the neck/shoulder level of the 5 ft 9 in figure) and approximately 3.5 to 4.0 ft wide.
